title: Trigger Patterns Schema
description: Schema for .claude/metadata/trigger-patterns.json — the phrase patterns workflow-trigger.js recognizes on UserPromptSubmit, plus the routing notes it appends when a route fires (#2999). This file carries PATTERNS and NOTES ONLY. The relationships between triggers — a co-required issue reference, and the mutual exclusions that stop `work #42` routing as an analysis request — stay in the hook, because expressing them here would need an evaluation order and a resolver for a three-entry dependency graph in a hook that must never throw. See Construction/Design-Decisions/2026-09-07-trigger-patterns-composition-stays-in-code.md.

version.description: Schema revision of this data file

_meta.description: Human-facing provenance. Never read by the hook.

analysisKeywords.description: Keywords that, combined with an issue reference, mark a prompt as analysis rather than work. Matched as WHOLE WORDS of the lowercased prompt (#3065) — 'check' does not match inside 'checklist' or 'checkout'. The hook still excludes competing triggers explicitly rather than relying on these keywords being disjoint, and exempts harness-generated prompts via the harnessFrame pattern (#3163).

commandRequests.description: Exact prompts (lowercased, --refresh stripped) that request the command help surface rather than routing to a command.

patterns.description: Named regular expressions. A name present here with an unparseable source is a broken pattern; a name ABSENT is a trigger the hook cannot evaluate at all, and the hook treats that as 'this trigger does not fire' rather than substituting a built-in. Keeping no fallback copy in code is what stops the two sources drifting.

source.description: Regular expression source, as accepted by the RegExp constructor. Written without delimiters.

flags.description: Regular expression flags. Omitted means no flags — distinct from an empty string only in intent, and the hook treats both identically.

description.description: What this pattern is for, and where its looseness or strictness is load-bearing.

routingNotes.description: Routing conventions the hook appends to its additionalContext when a route fires (#2999) — moved out of the always-on 02-github-workflow rule so a session sees each one only in the turn it applies. OPTIONAL by design: absent, malformed or empty, the hook emits its [INVOKE: …] line exactly as before. Routing never depends on a note.

notes.description: Note bodies keyed by id. A note shared by several routes (the flag pass-through convention) is written once and named by each.

text.description: Markdown appended verbatim after the hook's own payload. Must not contain a hook marker such as [INVOKE: — consumers grep the payload for it.

routes.description: Which notes each hook route appends, in order. Keys are the hook's route names, not pattern names.
